passages.title: My summer as a camp leader
passages.text:
Last summer I worked as a group leader at an adventure camp for teenagers in Scotland, and it was the best job I have (1) ______ had. I was responsible (2) ______ a group of twelve children aged between eleven and fourteen. Every morning I had to wake them up, make sure they ate a good breakfast and then take them to their activities, most (3) ______ which were outdoors. We went kayaking on the lake, climbed rocks and learnt how to build a fire safely.

The days were long and tiring. Some evenings I was (4) ______ exhausted that I fell asleep before the children did! The hardest part was looking after the ones who felt homesick. One boy, Callum, cried every night during his first week. I spent a lot of time talking to him and finding games he enjoyed, and by the end of the camp he was (5) ______ of the happiest children there.

I also made some great friends among the other leaders, and we still chat online most weeks. (6) ______ soon as applications open again, I'm going to apply for next summer.

questions.question: Write ONE word to fill gap (1).
questions.explanation: After a superlative with the present perfect we use 'ever': 'the best job I have ever had'. 'Never' would give the opposite meaning and is not possible after 'the best'.

questions.question: Write ONE word to fill gap (2).
questions.explanation: The adjective 'responsible' is always followed by 'for': 'I was responsible for a group of twelve children'.

questions.question: Write ONE word to fill gap (3).
questions.explanation: The relative phrase is 'most of which': 'their activities, most of which were outdoors', meaning that most of the activities took place outside.

questions.question: Write ONE word to fill gap (4).
questions.explanation: The structure 'so + adjective + that' shows a result: 'I was so exhausted that I fell asleep before the children did'. 'Such' is used before a noun, not an adjective alone, and 'too' cannot be followed by 'that'.

questions.question: Write ONE word to fill gap (5).
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative and a plural noun: 'one of the happiest children'. By the end of the camp Callum was very happy, which contrasts with how he cried every night in his first week.

questions.question: Write ONE word to fill gap (6).
questions.explanation: The time expression is 'as soon as', meaning 'immediately when': 'As soon as applications open again, I'm going to apply'. No other word can come before 'soon as' here.
